description: The University of Bristol hPET deposit publishes global land-surface potential evapotranspiration at 0.1-degree resolution with hourly and daily NetCDF files. Its own page lists years from 1981 onward, describes an annual update plan and reports a total archive size of 2.5 TiB. The values are calculated from ERA5-Land climate variables using the FAO Penman-Monteith formula. Irrigation, drought or reservoir simulations can use hPET as an atmospheric water-demand input. It estimates potential loss, not observed actual crop transpiration or water withdrawal, and source-weather and formula assumptions limit local accuracy. The provider page states CC BY 4.0. I read named metadata and a file-list sample without downloading data or checking each year. Related calculation code is a separate public repository; no exact catalogue deposit was found. A limitation is that potential evapotranspiration can diverge from actual water loss where vegetation or soil moisture constrains it.
